description: Canonical interpretation of a backend operation result. Nolan 2026-09-17: do NOT normalize the three observed success shapes ({status:'ok'}, {success:true}, {status:'completed'}) into one field; they may describe different layers. Instead decompose every result into four independent proof dimensions. The UI projection derives PROVEN_COMPLETE only when the required underlying proofs exist. Transport acceptance is not persistence; execution is not verification.

_envelope.description: In-band maturity/proof envelope. Canonical placement: under _envelope.

execution_status.description: Whether the operation ran. 'ran' means it executed; 'not_run' means it was accepted but never executed; 'failed' means it executed and failed.

interpreted_from.description: The raw backend shape this was interpreted from, e.g. '{status:ok}', '{success:true}', '{status:completed}'. Preserved, never rewritten.

persistence_status.description: Whether the result was durably recorded. 'skipped' covers cases like emit() on a null pool returning {status:'ok'} without an INSERT. A required write with skipped persistence can never derive PROVEN_COMPLETE.

proven_complete.description: Derived only. True iff every proof dimension the operation requires is satisfied: for a write, execution ran AND persistence persisted AND verification verified. The UI must use this field, never the raw backend shape, when rendering completion.

required_persistence.description: Whether persistence is required for this operation to count as complete. Writes: true. Pure reads/transport acceptance: false.

transport_status.description: Transport/acceptance layer: the request was accepted or rejected by the receiving runtime. Acceptance proves nothing about execution or persistence.

verification_status.description: Whether the persisted result was read back and checked.

title: OperationResult
